chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Husayn ibn Zayd, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The private parts are made permissible by three: marriage by inheritance, and marriage without inheritance, and marriage of the possession of the right hand.

key_terms.الْفَرْجُ: The private parts, referring to sexual organs; here metonymically for sexual relations.
key_terms.بِلَا مِيرَاثٍ: Without inheritance, referring to the standard contractual marriage.
key_terms.بِمِلْكِ الْيَمِينِ: By the possession of the right hand, referring to female slaves owned by the master.
key_terms.بِمِيرَاثٍ: By inheritance, referring to the wife who remains married to the husband after his death until the end of her waiting period.

ai.seo_question: What are the three ways sexual relations are made permissible in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) categorizes the three valid modes of lawful intimacy (halal) as permanent marriage, inheritance of a wife, and ownership of a slave girl (milk al-yamin). This classification reflects the classical Shia juristic view that these are the exclusive channels for permissibility, distinguishing them from illicit relations (zina). The inclusion of inheritance highlights the unique legal status of a widow as both an heir and a potential spouse for her deceased husband's heir, while milk al-yamin contextualizes the pre-modern practice of concubinage within the broader framework of marital law.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al Husay Bin Zayd who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The private Parts are Made to be Permissible by three – a marriage by inheritance, and a marriage without inheritance, and a marriage of the possession of the right hand (slave girl)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from al-Husayn ibn Zayd who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Marriage becomes lawful with three conditions: marriage with the right for inheritance, without inheritance, and with the right for ownership.’”
